assessment.nobel_worthiness: Converting a small molecule into a recruiter of the cell's ubiquitin-proteasome machinery is a clear molecular design principle: bifunctional PROTACs and monovalent molecular glues give precise control over protein-protein recognition and make previously undruggable proteins targetable. The idea is original, conceptually clean and has spread across chemical biology, medicinal chemistry and drug discovery. From my chemical-biology and translational viewpoint it passes the test of changing what researchers and clinicians can actually do.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept (2001) and Crews drove its chemical development. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target underlies the molecular-glue branch. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray and others contributed important later steps (VHL ligands, cell-active degraders), so the three-person limit leaves out real contributors and the glue and PROTAC branches could be argued as separate discoveries.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of work, many independent groups, and multiple degraders in advanced clinical trials give strong chemical confirmation. Approval of a PROTAC drug is still pending, so some clinical validation lags the chemistry, but the field looks ripe rather than premature.
uncertainties: Unclear whether the committee would prefer the PROTAC (Crews/Deshaies) or the molecular-glue (Handa) route as the core; I rely on memory for exact clinical status.
Attribution among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli and others is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable cationic lipids that are neutral in circulation and charged in the acidic endosome, formulated into lipid nanoparticles, solved the delivery problem for siRNA and mRNA. This is a molecular design principle (pKa tuning of lipid headgroups) that enabled approved siRNA drugs and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, an unusually large, concrete change in what clinicians can do. The underlying lipid chemistry has not been recognised by the Medicine prize for nucleoside-modified mRNA.
assessment.attribution: Cullis led the LNP formulation and ionizable-lipid concept; MacLachlan contributed to the SNALP/ionizable-lipid development at Inex/Tekmira; Anderson and Langer drove combinatorial lipid-like materials and later optimization. Hope and Madden were early co-inventors. Patent history and disputes obscure who made the decisive step, so allocation is genuinely unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Very mature in clinical impact with billions of doses and several approved products. Fundamental mechanistic understanding of endosomal escape and targeting is still incomplete, but this does not undermine the recognition of the delivery chemistry.
uncertainties: Credit is fragmented among at least six names with commercial and patent conflicts.
Whether the committee views this as chemistry or as pharmaceutics/medicine.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs that incorporate unnatural amino acids site-specifically in living cells give chemists atom-level control over protein composition, enabling new probes, crosslinkers, bioorthogonal handles and engineered biologics. It is original, general and widely adopted across chemical biology and biomaterials, and it connects naturally to designed peptide and protein building blocks.
assessment.attribution: Schultz (with Wang) established the first in vivo expansion in E. coli and eukaryotes; Chin extended it to orthogonal ribosomes, quadruplet codons and genomically recoded organisms. Mehl and Yokoyama made substantial contributions, so three names cannot cover all decisive work.
assessment.maturity: Twenty-plus years of independent reproduction and widespread use, plus therapeutic applications now emerging. The field is mature, and the question is whether it is still fresh relative to other candidates.
uncertainties: Overlap with other recognised prizes (directed evolution, bioorthogonal chemistry) could be thought to reduce novelty.
Relative weight of Schultz vs Chin vs Wang is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat showed that the mutant cysteine of KRAS G12C can be targeted covalently through a cryptic pocket (and earlier developed chemical genetics with analog-sensitive kinases). KRAS was long regarded as undruggable, and the resulting approved drugs, such as sotorasib and adagrasib, are a clear case of a chemical insight changing clinical oncology.
assessment.attribution: Shokat's lab made the decisive discovery of the tethering-based KRAS G12C inhibitors. Drug development in industry (Amgen, Mirati, others) built on this, and Ostrem/Shokat's contribution is clearly identifiable. A single-laureate configuration is natural, but a shared prize with a second chemical-genetics or covalent-drugging pioneer is possible.
assessment.maturity: Approved drugs and a wave of follow-on KRAS inhibitors confirm the concept. Durability of clinical responses is limited by resistance, but the chemical principle is secure.
uncertainties: Single-person candidate; the committee may prefer combining with other chemical biology topics.
Resistance and modest durability could temper enthusiasm.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors fuse a deaminase to a Cas protein to chemically convert one base into another without double-strand cleavage, an elegant protein-engineering and chemistry approach that offers precision beyond CRISPR nuclease editing. It has rapidly become a core genome-engineering tool with first clinical use.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual and experimental work, with Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor) as the leading first authors. A Liu-centred prize is the most defensible allocation. Chemistry already recognised CRISPR-Cas9 in 2020, which raises sequencing and scope questions.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent adoption and early clinical data, but the long-term clinical record is limited. Timeliness is plausible but perhaps early relative to 2020 recognition of genome editing.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a sufficiently distinct step after the 2020 prize.
Clinical safety data are still short; off-target and bystander editing issues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle for membraneless compartments reframed how cells organise biochemistry and brought physical-chemical concepts (multivalency, polymer physics) into cell biology. As a molecular physicist I value that a physical principle, not a single molecule, explains cellular organisation, and I see strong ties to peptide self-assembly and biomaterials.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman provided the 2009 P-granule demonstration; Rosen and Pappu contributed the multivalent-interaction and sequence-grammar framework. Three names can cover it, but Pappu and Mittag are strong alternatives, so credit is debated.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted but controversial in places: in vivo relevance, definitions and artefacts from overexpression are still argued. Concept is influential but may be premature for a prize.
uncertainties: Debated in vivo physiological relevance and terminology.
It is an organising concept rather than a discrete chemical discovery, which may fall outside a strict chemistry reading.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminator nucleotides and single-molecule clustered arrays transformed biology and medicine, making genomes cheap enough for routine clinical use. The chemistry of fluorescent reversible terminators is an elegant molecular design solution with enormous translational impact.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived the Solexa approach and its chemistry. Others (Ju, Rothberg, Mayer) developed competing or complementary methods, so recognition could become contested. Two names is a coherent configuration.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature; technology is the basis of large-scale genomics. Recognition is overdue rather than premature, though the 1980 prize was for sequencing methods and Sanger's chemistry was already honoured.
uncertainties: Competing methods (454, Ju, Mayer) complicate credit.
Whether the committee regards it as chemistry or as technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed assembly of gold nanoparticles and spherical nucleic acids provide programmable recognition at the nanoscale, enabling colorimetric biosensing, intracellular gene regulation and materials with designed lattices. The work uses precisely controlled molecular recognition to drive assembly, closely tied to my own peptide-nanoparticle and plasmonic biosensing field.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin's group and Alivisatos's group independently published the 1996 DNA-gold nanoparticle assembly papers; Mirkin extended this to spherical nucleic acids. Alivisatos has less direct connection to the later SNA developments, so the pairing is imperfect and Mirkin is the central figure.
assessment.maturity: Mature in diagnostics and materials, with commercial products. Therapeutic SNAs are still in early clinical development, so the evidence of broad biomedical transformation is mixed.
uncertainties: Alivisatos might better be recognised for semiconductor nanocrystals, already honoured in 2023.
Limited independent consensus on therapeutic impact.
